answer: Require each identity to bind to one trusted execution environment whose remote-attestation quote carries a hardware-rooted unique key. A chip can back only one registration; a later quote from the same silicon is refused, and fresh-nonce re-attestation each epoch blocks replay. A hollow quote from a shared or simulated enclave burns the locked deposit, a marble of stake reserved at enrollment. An island operator with one real enclave keeps full weight; a warehouse of cloned identities collapses into a single seat.
